description.narrative: Projektet ”Fostering Employment and Growth Opportunities”, FEGO, syftar till att stödja den utveckling som äger rum inom den privata sektorn i fråga om ökad sysselsättning och skapande av egenföretagande bland ungdomar, kvinnor och minoritetsgrupper. Projektet fokuserar på att ge katalytiskt stöd till utvecklingen av mikro- och småföretag inom kläd- och möbelsektorerna, företagsinitiativ för företagande samt utveckling av landsbygdsturism i Kosovo. Den föreslagna insatsen ska genomföras av Swisscontact Foundation. Insatsen bygger på metoden för marknadssystemutveckling (MSD) som inkluderar ett systemiskt, adaptivt och innovativt förhållningssätt. Centralt är lokalt ägda lösningar från olika aktörer i de utvalda sektorerna och områdena

The Fostering Employment and Growth Opportunities (FEGO) project aims at supporting private sector development-led employment and self-employment creation, amongst youth, women and minority communities. The project will catalyze these employment opportunities through two main outcomes, namely the growth and development of micro and small enterprises in the apparel and furniture sectors and business-to-business entrepreneurship initiatives as well as development of rural tourism in Kosovo. The proposed intervention will be implemented by Swisscontact foundation. The intervention is based on market system development (MSD) approach that include a systemic and adaptive approach, innovative, with locally owned solutions by engaging different actors in the selected sectors.

The overall objective of the proposed intervention is job creation and income generation in the furniture, apparel, and rural tourism sectors, to contribute to addressing high unemployment and poverty rates in the country, especially amongst youth and women.
Its specific objective is to facilitate growth and performance improvement in the micro and small and start-up businesses in the apparel, furniture, and rural tourism sectors, and contribute to the emergence of more extensive opportunities for income generation and employment amongst presently poor and socio-economically excluded women, men and youth.
Specific objective 2: Scaling up trade interventions: 1.Participating in and facilitating pivotal export fairs promotion, targeted buyers, and familiarization trips 2.An Export Fund mechanism for supporting exporting enterprises 3.Facilitating capacity-building programs for sector associations and MSMEs in the furniture and apparel sectors.

The four year implementation of the FEGO project (20222025) by Swisscontact marks a major structural shift in Kosovos private sector. Rather than temporarily patching over structural gaps with short-term fixes or direct subsidies, the project successfully used an Inclusive Systems Development (ISD) approach. By treating local businesses, municipalities, and industry groups as active partners who invested their own money through a facilitation model, FEGO permanently fixed production delays, brought in private funding, and built a self-sustaining business community that can grow on its own.
Results to highlight, expected and unexpected
An evaluation of the project's data shows that the expected results not only met targets but consistently beat them. On the expected front, FEGO actively supported 324 small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) across the furniture, apparel, and rural tourism sectors, reaching 120% of its initial project target of 270 businesses. This growth directly helped local families, as total worker earnings jumped to €6.45 million, beating the project target of €4.5 million by 143%. Participating businesses also generated €5.56 million in extra sales and exports, hitting 104% of their €7.0 million economic target. Furthermore, the project drove the creation of 870 new jobs, coming close to its total target of 900 people employed and benefiting (97% of the target reached when including expected post-2025 impacts). The project focused heavily on inclusion; in 2025 alone, 379 new jobs were created, and 59% (222 jobs) went to women while 68% (257 jobs) went to young people. At the factory level, apparel businesses used co-investments to buy automated sewing, textile printing, and embroidery machines to speed up production and stop relying on outsourcing. Meanwhile, furniture factories upgraded heavy woodworking machinery to eliminate manufacturing bottlenecks. In rural tourism, the project helped launch 40 new small tourism businesses over the last four years in emerging destinations like Ferizaj and Kamenica, comparing empty or undeveloped local markets to a newly diversified sector offering mountain e-biking, zip-lines, and physical route signage for the "Mother Teresa Walking Trail".
Alongside these planned milestones, the project triggered several highly successful unexpected results. First, the co-investment strategy smashed expectations by leveraging €4.64 million in private sector and municipal investments, beating the original project target of €1.9 million by a staggering 244%. Second, a major unexpected spillover effect occurred when competing businesses that never received project help began copying FEGO's business models. To stay competitive against FEGO's network, these outside firms independently invested in similar technologies and efficient production habits. Third, local apparel businesses unexpectedly took over high-value niche markets, such as custom embroidery for the domestic hospitality sector, capturing revenues that had previously been almost entirely imported from other countries. Finally, the project's innovation fund successfully stepped outside of tourism to help a major shoe factory build its own in-house insole production line, which fixed a hidden supply chain link and successfully reduced its reliance on foreign imports.
